answers.answer: Shuffle each player’s separate 30-card deck and draw 5; set heroes and sidekicks to their stated starting health (undialed sidekicks have 1). Younger player places hero on space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; if the hero’s space is in multiple zones, any of those zones qualifies. Alice chooses BIG or SMALL at her placement. Older player then places hero on space 2 and sidekicks by the same rule. Younger player goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup: “each player shuffles their 30 action cards into one separate face-down deck, then draws 5”; younger places on 1, older on 2; sidekicks use separate spaces sharing a zone; Alice chooses size when placing.

answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, or attack. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice, but cannot skip an action. You may hold 9 during the turn; at its end discard 2 cards to your own discard pile until you have 7.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “take 2 actions”; “You may repeat an action”; “you cannot skip an action”; “At the end of your turn, discard excess cards ... until you have 7.”

answers.answer: Maneuver draws 1 card first, mandatorily, then each of your fighters may move independently up to that player’s move value (plus applicable bonuses), including zero. Move one fighter at a time and finish that fighter’s move before starting another. You may pass through friendly fighters, not opposing fighters, and may not finish on any occupied space.
answers.evidence: Maneuver: “Draw 1 card first, mandatory”; each fighter moves independently; friendly pass-through allowed, opposing pass-through prohibited, no occupied destination; finish each fighter before starting the next.

answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard one card from hand and add its printed BOOST value to the movement value for that maneuver. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. Every one of your fighters receives that movement allowance. A card unusable because its fighter is defeated can still be discarded to BOOST.
answers.evidence: BOOST movement: discard 1 card, add its circled BOOST value, “Each of your fighters receives that allowance”; ignore effects; defeated fighter’s unusable card can still BOOST.

answers.answer: Do not reshuffle and do not decline a mandatory draw. Both draws are missing, so each surviving fighter takes 2 damage for each missing card: 4 damage per fighter total (hero and sidekick), unless hero defeat ends the game during resolution.
answers.evidence: Empty deck: “Do not reshuffle”; each time unable to draw, each fighter immediately takes 2 damage instead. A mandatory draw of 2 with empty deck causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat ends the game.

answers.answer: A melee fighter may attack any adjacent opponent, including across zone boundaries, but cannot attack a nonadjacent target even in the same zone or a disconnected part of it. A ranged fighter may attack an adjacent opponent across zones, or any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance or adjacency, including in a disconnected part of that colored zone.
answers.evidence: Attack: any fighter can attack an adjacent opponent across zone boundaries; melee only adjacent; ranged also any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance or adjacency, including separated parts.

answers.answer: An attack action is illegal if you have no attack-capable card in hand or none of your fighters has a valid target. Name your attacking fighter and the opposing fighter targeted. The attacker plays a legal attack card for that fighter; defender may decline or play a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Reveal both choices simultaneously after both have chosen. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects.
answers.evidence: Attack section: attack action prerequisites, active attacker and target declaration, legal card labels, defender may decline, simultaneous reveal; versatile cards “count as both attack and defense cards for other effects.”

answers.answer: Resolve immediately card effects; then during-combat effects; determine combat damage and winner; resolve after-combat card effects; resolve other after-combat game effects (such as a hero special ability); finally put all played cards into their respective discard piles. When effects share a timing, defender resolves first. Card effects are mandatory unless explicitly optional and are completed in printed order.
answers.evidence: Combat timing, damage and winning combat lists the six steps; “Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first”; effects mandatory unless they say otherwise; played cards finally enter respective discard piles.

answers.answer: The defender wins combat: the attack dealt zero damage, and effect damage does not change the combat winner. The later 2 effect damage does not make the attacker the winner. With no defense card, attack damage is 4.
answers.evidence: “attacker wins combat only if the attack itself deals at least 1 damage”; damage from effects does not change winner. With no defense card, defender takes attack value.

answers.answer: A defeated sidekick token is immediately removed. If the game continues because its hero lives, that defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects. If a hero reaches zero, that player immediately loses and the game ends; do not continue pending effects to heal the hero or finish the turn.
answers.evidence: Victory: defeated sidekick token is immediately removed; defeated hero immediately loses and game ends. Combat timing: defeated fighter’s played card still resolves after-combat effects unless game already ended.

answers.answer: Play a scheme face up from hand, naming an active fighter permitted by its fighter label; you cannot play it if its listed fighter is defeated. Resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile. Both players may inspect either face-up discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Scheme: play face up, declare a fighter permitted by label, cannot play if listed fighters are defeated, resolve then discard. Cards section: both players may inspect either discard pile at any time.

answers.answer: Alice starts at 13 health, moves 2, and is melee. Jabberwock starts at 8 health, is melee, and uses Alice’s sidekick move value of 2 during maneuver. Alice chooses BIG or SMALL when placed at setup. BIG adds 2 to Alice’s attack-card values; SMALL adds 1 to Alice’s defense-card values, including versatile cards used in that role. Neither bonus applies to Jabberwock.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Alice 13/melee/move 2 and Jabberwock 8/melee; move applies to each fighter. Alice ability states bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.

answers.answer: Arthur starts at 18 health and is melee; Merlin starts at 7 and is ranged. Both use move 2. When Arthur attacks, he may play a hand card face down alongside his attack card, add its BOOST value, ignore its effects, and discard it. If the opponent cancels effects on Arthur’s attack card, this ability’s BOOST is discarded without effect.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference and Arthur ability: Arthur 18/melee, Merlin 7/ranged; both move 2; attack BOOST method and cancellation consequence stated.

answers.answer: Medusa starts at 16 health, moves 3, and is ranged. She has 3 Harpies, each with 1 health and melee attack. At the start of Medusa’s turn, she may deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone; this is optional, requires no adjacency, and Harpies do not project it from their zones.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Medusa and 3 Harpies; Medusa ability states optional 1 damage to an opposing fighter in her zone at start of turn, no adjacency, not projected by Harpies.

answers.answer: Sinbad and Porter each start at 2 normal move; Sinbad has 15 health and melee attack, Porter 6 health and melee attack. With 3 Voyage cards already in the discard pile, each gets +3, so each may move up to 5 spaces before any maneuver BOOST. A newly played base-2 Voyage has combat value 5 (2 plus the 3 other Voyages already discarded); it does not count itself because it enters the discard pile only at the end of combat.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference supplies stats and move. Sinbad ability gives +1 movement per Voyage in discard for each fighter, and Voyage combat value +1 per other Voyage in discard; played cards enter discard only at end of combat.

answers.answer: Eat Me moves Alice up to 3 spaces, then changes her size, even if she moved zero. Drink Me draws 2 cards, then changes her size. The size change is not optional: both effects direct it without “may,” and effects are mandatory unless stated otherwise.
answers.evidence: Card reference gives Eat Me and Drink Me effects; general rule says card effects are mandatory unless otherwise stated; Alice rule says change size is mandatory when effect says so.

answers.answer: No attack damage is dealt (4 attack versus 4 defense), so Arthur wins combat. The defender’s after-combat Skirmish resolves first and moves Jabberwock up to 2 spaces; in the given setup it leaves no adjacent fighter. Then Jaws That Bite checks adjacency and deals no damage because none is adjacent. If only a friendly fighter were adjacent, Jaws’ 2 damage would be mandatory and would hit that fighter; Alice cannot decline it.
answers.evidence: Combat winner is based on attack damage, not equality of card values; same-timing defender resolves first. Timing example directly describes this 4-versus-4 sequence and Jaws adjacency; Jaws effect says damage is mandatory even if only target is friendly.

answers.answer: At 4 health, Arthur is alive and at 4 or less, so The Holy Grail sets his health to 8. At 5, nothing happens. At 0, hero defeat has already ended the duel, so the pending after-combat healing does not resolve. Recovery cannot exceed a fighter’s dial maximum.
answers.evidence: The Holy Grail: if Arthur has 4 or less but is not defeated, set to 8; at 5+ nothing; at 0 duel already ended. Recovery cannot exceed dial maximum.

answers.answer: Winged Frenzy lets each of Medusa’s fighters move up to 3 spaces and pass through opposing fighters. Then, if any Harpy is defeated, return one defeated Harpy to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone. It cannot end on an occupied space.
answers.evidence: Winged Frenzy effect specifies each own fighter, up to 3, may pass through opponents, then return a defeated Harpy if any to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone.

answers.answer: During combat, Voyage Home is worth 6 (base 2 plus 1 for each of 4 other Voyages in the discard pile); it does not count itself. After combat, it returns all 4 other Voyages from Sinbad’s discard pile to his hand. Voyage Home itself then goes to the discard pile at the normal end of combat. For his next unboosted maneuver, only Voyage Home is in the discard pile, so Sinbad and Porter each have allowance 3 (normal move 2 plus 1).
answers.evidence: Voyages are Sinbad-only A/2 and get +1 per other Voyage in discard; card currently played is not yet there. Voyage Home takes all other Voyages from discard into hand, then Home itself goes to discard at normal end; maneuver bonus also applies to Porter.
